investigation.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: LLM provider returned overloaded_error via POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed at 2026-08-31T17:16:25.108Z when POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "harness runtime test failed (llm_error): provider returned invalid event shape: overloaded_error: Overloaded". Because the LLM provider returned an overload error instead of a valid streaming event, the harness received no usable response, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were absent from the eval result. This is an eval infrastructure failure against a transient provider-side condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream LLM provider returned an overloaded_error event during the runtime test call. The harness classified this as an invalid event shape (llm_error) and surfaced it as a 502 bad_gateway to the eval runner. Because the call never completed successfully, the probe received no response body from which to extract orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 102–105) to fail with all five required evidence fields missing. The failure is localized to the POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test endpoint and the LLM provider layer it depends on; agent creation and permissions checks passed in the same run, confirming that the AURA API, agent lifecycle, and permissions subsystems were healthy at the time.

The failure is localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner logic or the API surface itself.

investigations.rootCause: The upstream LLM provider returned an overloaded_error event during the runtime test call. The harness classified this as an invalid event shape (llm_error) and surfaced it as a 502 bad_gateway to the eval runner. Because the call never completed successfully, the probe received no response body from which to extract orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 102–105) to fail with all five required evidence fields missing. The failure is localized to the POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test endpoint and the LLM provider layer it depends on; agent creation and permissions checks passed in the same run, confirming that the AURA API, agent lifecycle, and permissions subsystems were healthy at the time.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agents eval group that verifies swarm gateway reachability and skips downstream checks with a clear SKIP message if the gateway is unreachable, rather than failing all checks with a 502.

Add a historical baseline eval that tracks consecutive failure counts for remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state against the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold, so a sustained gateway outage triggers an automated alert before the second consecutive failure window.
